audit.whatIsWrong: Rated TRICKY 7.5/10 on a 50.26% win rate where the packet chart hands Gangplank levels 6, first item and 2+ items.
audit.why: Losing levels 1-3 to a tank you out-scale is not a 7.5/10 lane; the rating told the player to play scared through a stage he wins.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, tone amber, diffRating 6/10, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] realigned.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts were wrong at five of seven rows and inverted at the ends: Level 1 given to Gangplank when the content says 'Levels 1-3 belong to Malphite', and First item and 2+ items given to Malphite when the content says Sheen flips the lane and 'your scaling keg carry pattern beats a tank who built only armor'.
audit.why: The chart claimed Gangplank wins the stage he loses and loses the two stages he wins — the exact inverse of the article and of the packet.
audit.corrected: win[0], win[2], win[3], win[5], win[6] and phases[0], [2], [3], [5], [6] side/rating/why brought onto the packet chart as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and dosFull[0] all describe Unstoppable Force as 'un-dodgeable burst' — the content layer of the same matchup correctly says it is a dash-charge you can sidestep or Flash. The full layer also never mentions Granite Shield, which absorbs 10% of his max health and RECHARGES if he goes a few seconds without being hit — the single most important thing about poking him.
audit.why: 'Un-dodgeable' tells the player not to try to dodge the one ability in this matchup he can dodge, and the two layers of the same page contradicted each other. Missing the shield recharge means poking on a timer that gives it back for free.
audit.corrected: Full layer rebuilt: R is 130s at rank 1, 1000 range, and dodgeable; Granite Shield's 10% and its recharge now drive the poke advice; Thunderclap named as the auto-reset tell in the trading blocks.

notes: The two layers of this page directly contradicted each other on the decisive ability: the content correctly calls Unstoppable Force a dodgeable dash-charge, the full layer called it 'un-dodgeable burst' three times. Resolved in the content's favour, which also matches the mirror audit. Following the mirror's finding, I made no claim about whether Remove Scurvy can strip the knock-up — the kit files do not answer it — and I did not write the derived 'grounding' flags on Seismic Shard or Ground Slam, since Riot's descriptions do not support them. The content layer here was already in good shape and needed almost nothing.
